Bill.BriefDescription: Authorizing fees for initial medicare certification surveys conducted by the department of health.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to fees for initial medicare certification surveysconducted by the department of health; and amending RCW 43.70.125.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 43.70.125 and 2007 c 279 s 1 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText:
(1) The federal government requires Washington health carefacilities to be certified in order to receive federal health careprogram reimbursement. The department receives funding from thefederal government to perform the ((certifications andrecertifications)) initial medicare certification surveys of thesehealth care facilities. When the federal government does not providesufficient funding to cover all ((certifications and recertifications))applicant requests for initial medicare certification surveys, thesecretary ((may)) must assess fees on ((certification andrecertification)) the applicants to fund the ((certifications andrecertifications)) initial medicare certification surveys, as providedin this section. (2)(a) When informed by the department that the centers for p. 1 HB 2296medicare and medicaid services did not provide adequate federal fundingto do initial medicare certification surveys, an applicant for a surveymay pay the department a fee to conduct the survey as follows:
Ambulatory surgery center$1,575
Critical access hospital$1,750
Endstage renal diseasefacility$850
Home health agency$1,985
Hospice agency$1,985
Hospital$1,750
Rehabilitation facility$450
Rural health clinic$600
Transplant hospital$850 (b) If the applicant does not pay the fee, the department has noobligation to conduct the initial medicare certification surveys. (3) Nothing in this section precludes an applicant from obtainingan initial medicare certification survey from a national accreditationorganization recognized for this purpose by the centers for medicareand medicaid services. (4) For the purposes of this section, "initial medicarecertification survey" means an onsite visit conducted by departmentstaff for the purpose of determining compliance with medicareregulations. This survey is required before a health care facility canreceive medicare or medicaid reimbursement.
